challenges.title: The shared document invitation
challenges.briefing: You receive a document-sharing email at Alder Design. Your company uses docs.alder.example for internal documents. Review the invitation before opening it.
challenges.evidence:
From: Document Support <sharing@alder-docs.example>
Subject: Your manager shared the updated rota

Open the document at https://docs.alder.example.access-check.example/rota

To unlock access, enter your password and the latest six-digit MFA code. Do not open your usual document portal; this file uses a special access flow.
challenges.question: Which action best protects your account?
options: Open the familiar document portal independently and verify the invitation with your manager
Enter only the MFA code because it expires quickly
Trust the link because its address starts with docs.alder.example
Forward the link to colleagues so they can test it
challenges.explanation: The link belongs to access-check.example, not alder.example. Familiar text earlier in a hostname does not establish ownership. The request for a password and MFA code through an unusual flow is another warning. Open the known portal independently and verify the request through a trusted channel.
challenges.takeaway: Check the actual destination domain and never supply credentials or MFA codes through an unverified invitation.

challenges.title: A backup outside the allowlist
challenges.briefing: The approved backup client uses source 192.0.2.10 between 01:00 and 01:15 UTC. The service account should not be used elsewhere. Review these object-storage audit events.
challenges.evidence:
01:03:10 user=svc_backup src=192.0.2.10 action=READ object=backup/current.tar result=ALLOW
12:15:04 user=svc_backup src=198.51.100.27 action=LIST bucket=customer-exports result=ALLOW
12:15:08 user=svc_backup src=198.51.100.27 action=READ object=customer-exports/full.csv result=ALLOW
12:15:12 user=svc_backup src=198.51.100.27 action=READ object=customer-exports/archive.csv result=ALLOW
challenges.question: Which finding most clearly warrants investigation?
options: A backup occurred inside the approved time window
The service account read a file at 01:03 UTC
Every event has an ALLOW result so none is suspicious
The service account accessed customer exports from an unapproved source outside its scheduled window
challenges.explanation: The midday requests violate both the documented source restriction and the expected backup window, and access customer-export files. An ALLOW result records a successful authorisation decision, not proof that the activity was legitimate. Preserve the logs and investigate the account and credentials before concluding how access occurred.
challenges.takeaway: Compare service-account activity against its expected source, time and purpose; a successful request can still be suspicious.

challenges.title: Whose invoice is it?
challenges.briefing: This endpoint requires a signed-in user. Invoice IDs are unique but appear in customer emails. The handler currently checks no ownership before returning a record.
challenges.question: Which fix directly addresses the missing security check?
options: Make invoice IDs longer and rely on them staying secret
Check that invoice.ownerUserId matches req.user.id before returning the record
Require users to refresh the page before requesting an invoice
Hide the invoice link in the navigation menu
challenges.explanation: Signing in establishes identity but does not grant access to every invoice. The server must enforce ownership or an explicit authorised role before returning a record. Longer IDs and hidden links do not replace this check. A query scoped by both invoice ID and current user is also a valid implementation.
challenges.takeaway: Enforce authorisation for the specific object on the server, even when a route already requires sign-in.
